title: The Ethical Debt
subtitle: Why wasting animal data is wasting animal lives
thesis: The Ethical Debt of preclinical research: animals are used to generate knowledge, but the resulting data are allowed to become unusable. Data welfare is animal welfare.

strongest_evidence.claim: Publication bias and excess significance inflate apparent efficacy in animal disease-model literature (e.g. stroke efficacy falling from 31.2% to 23.8%; 1,719 significant results observed vs 919 expected in neurological models).
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Based on systematic CAMARADES meta-analyses of thousands of datasets with quantitative trim-and-fill/Egger and excess-significance tests, full-text verified, and convergent across two independent analyses (Sena 2010; Tsilidis 2013).

weakest_evidence.claim: Cumulative preclinical irreproducibility is ~53% and costs US$28B/year.
weakest_evidence.why_weak: A modeled point estimate from a very wide probability-bounds range (18%-88.5%) built on a few non-transparent industry reports; the authors themselves note costs could be much smaller or larger.

evidence_gaps.topic: Irreproducibility cost estimates outside the US
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: The cited US$28B/year figure is US-only and modeled from bounded assumptions; comparable empirical cost estimates for Europe, Asia or globally are largely absent.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Policy and funding decisions on data reuse and FAIR rest on a single modeled figure whose sensitivity and generalizability are rarely tested.

evidence_gaps.topic: Primary experimental source for the headline preclinical irreproducibility percentages
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: The often-repeated 11% (Amgen) and 25% (Bayer) reproducibility rates are known only through secondary reporting; the underlying per-experiment datasets are not public.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: false_consensus_risk: field-defining statistics rest on non-transparent industry reports that cannot be independently audited.

evidence_gaps.topic: Link between non-publication of animal studies and downstream clinical harm
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Quantitative evidence connecting specific unpublished/negative animal studies to avoidable failed clinical trials or patient harm is sparse.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: The ethical (3Rs) and translational stakes of publication bias are asserted more often than measured.

cluster_02.name: The 3Rs, animal welfare ethics, and Reduction

strongest_evidence.claim: Conventional laboratory housing significantly worsens stress-sensitive disease and mortality in rodents relative to enriched housing, with medium-to-large effect sizes.
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Pre-registered random-effects meta-analysis of 214 studies and 6495 animals with quantified effect sizes and confidence intervals, and an explicit test showing enrichment did not inflate data variability.

weakest_evidence.claim: A 15-year NHP blood-marker dataset shows mildly-severe neuroscience procedures cause no long-term cumulative harm.
weakest_evidence.why_weak: Single-laboratory, single-species observational dataset (39 macaques) with no untreated longitudinal control group; a null result that cannot exclude cumulative effects on unmeasured welfare dimensions.

evidence_gaps.topic: Harm-benefit analysis accountability
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Prospective validation that project-level HBA reliably predicts realised benefit; almost all evidence is retrospective or theoretical.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: HBA is the legal cornerstone of animal-research regulation, yet its objectivity and predictive validity remain largely untested.

evidence_gaps.topic: Culture of care and research quality
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration that culture-of-care programmes or staff wellbeing improve animal welfare or data quality.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Culture of care is being written into policy and frameworks on the assumption of a wellbeing-to-quality link that has not been measured (false_consensus_risk).

evidence_gaps.topic: Cumulative severity
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Longitudinal, species-general objective biomarkers of cumulative lifetime harm; current evidence is single-species and often contradictory (e.g. NHP blood markers show no cumulative effect while telomere models predict one).
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Directive 2010/63/EU requires assessment of cumulative severity but validated cross-species tools are lacking.

evidence_gaps.topic: Efficacy of standard analgesia protocols (Refinement)
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Evidence that commonly used analgesics (e.g. buprenorphine, meloxicam) actually prevent pain rather than merely being administered; controlled studies show failure to prevent pain or drug-induced harm reaching humane endpoints.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Refinement is assumed to reduce suffering, but if standard analgesia is ineffective or harmful the welfare side of the harm-benefit analysis is overstated.

strongest_evidence.claim: Actual public availability of research data in medicine is extremely low (~2% actually shared vs ~8% declared) and voluntary/on-request mechanisms do not work, a pattern independently replicated across many specialties and audits.
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Convergent across a 105-study IPD meta-analysis and multiple independent single-field audits (BMJ 4.5%, oncology, gastroenterology, orthopaedics, BioMed Central author-contact study), with quantified effect sizes and consistent direction.

evidence_gaps.topic: FAIR data actually increasing reuse of preclinical/animal data

evidence_gaps.topic: Secondary use / repositories for long-tail preclinical animal data

cluster_05.name: Virtual control groups, historical controls, and control-data reuse

strongest_evidence.claim: Replacing concurrent controls with VCGs preserves study-level conclusions (NOAEL) but degrades reproducibility of individual clinical-pathology endpoints.
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Converging fulltext evidence from an independent simulation (10.3389/fphar.2026.1704002) and a review of two proof-of-concept studies (10.1177/01926233241300310), with quantified agreement and non-reproducibility rates from body text.

weakest_evidence.claim: VCGs can be extended to reduce control non-human primate use.
weakest_evidence.why_weak: Aspirational; no NHP VCG concordance data exist and the same review flags NHP variability as a barrier.

evidence_gaps.topic: Regulatory acceptance of VCGs
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: No published evidence of a regulatory authority accepting a VCG-based study in lieu of concurrent controls; VICT3R explicitly still seeks acceptance.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Without regulatory acceptance the animal-reduction benefit remains theoretical.

evidence_gaps.topic: VCG performance in non-rodent / NHP species
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Proof-of-concept studies are confined to rats; no quantitative VCG concordance data in dogs or non-human primates.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: The largest ethical payoff (NHP reduction) is exactly where variability and data gaps are greatest.

evidence_gaps.topic: Primary evidence that HCD temporal drift biases VCG conclusions
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Drift is documented at the covariate level (study year effect), but a direct demonstration that drift flips a NOAEL/hazard call is not clearly established.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: false_consensus_risk: the drift concern is widely repeated but its decision-level impact is inferred rather than directly measured.

evidence_gaps.topic: Cross-laboratory transferability of historical/virtual controls
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: A cardiovascular QTc study shows same-laboratory historical controls are usable but cross-laboratory vehicle controls are not, due to differing time-courses; no general method exists to make control data transferable across laboratories.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: VCG databases pool control data across companies/labs, so undocumented cross-lab differences could bias VCG-based decisions.

evidence_gaps.topic: IACUC/AWERB oversight effectiveness
